independent_course_basis.explanation: In selection sort, each pass finds the largest unsorted element and swaps it into its correct position at the end of the unsorted portion. After each pass, the sorted region grows by one element from the right, so the next pass must shrink its range regardless of whether a swap was needed—because the last examined position is now confirmed sorted. This invariant holds even if the largest element was already at the boundary.

checks.reason: The learner correctly infers that confirmation—not swapping—determines finality, consistent with the invariant described in the evidence.

checks.source_fact: After placing the largest element, the algorithm looks left of the red line, excluding the sorted portion from the next pass.
checks.learner_meaning: The next pass excludes the confirmed position, shrinking the unsorted range.
